A circuit breaker is a safety feature in electrical circuits that helps prevent overloads and prevents damage to the system. It works by detecting when a circuit is overloaded and shutting it down to protect the equipment and prevent damage.

When a circuit breaker trips, it stops the power supply to the affected circuit, shutting down the power to the connected devices. This prevents the overload from causing damage to the equipment, such as equipment, wiring, or other components.

Circuit breakers are typically used in homes, businesses, and industrial settings to protect against electrical faults and ensure the safety and reliability of the electrical system.
